assertions.description: Boot workflow state.yaml shows status: complete
Session index file exists — boot's Session Index Boot step must have created/appended it
Session index is a real record, not an empty stub
step-06.5's guardrail checkpoint recorded a result (pass/flag/escalate) on this run — read from the eval record's own guardrails array, not self-reported by the workflow
OmniFocus pull (step-01.2 Pull B) wrote its consolidated data file

OmniFocus pull did not report status:failed. This assertion surfaces the five consecutive degraded boots of September 2026, which were caused by treating the absent Desktop Commander tool as OmniFocus being unreachable. Both the OmniFocus MCP and osascript via the Bash tool work, and neither requires Desktop Commander.

No completed task leaked into the OmniFocus pull. The inbox permanently holds ~247 completed tasks alongside ~8 incomplete ones, and Clean Up does NOT remove them, so the query itself must carry `completed is false`. Any `completed: true` in the output means the filter was dropped from the call.

assertions.pattern: "completed"\s*:\s*false|completed is false|completed` MUST be present and false
assertions.description: Regression guard: the boot pull instructions still mandate the completed=false filter on the inbox query. Matches the JSON field form ("completed": false), the old prose form (`completed is false`), and the current canonical phrasing (`completed` MUST be present and false on every task) — the guard previously false-fired on the 2026-10-22 rewrite because the pattern had not been widened with it. If someone strips the filter entirely, this trips before the leak reaches a briefing.

Master J2 (routing correctness): no step on this run that belongs to a specialist workflow (per workflows/<name>/workflow.md's agent frontmatter) or to a specialist's boot-step range (per agents/manifest.md) may carry owning_agent: master. Fails if the coordinator is recorded as owning a specialist's step — e.g. a plaud-ingest step (owned by knox) stamped master. A step whose own workflow is master-owned (boot's own steps) or that the manifest assigns to master is not flagged. This is the routing-assertion hook J2's A/B evidence requires; it reads the manifest ownership table and the workflow step definitions, not self-reported claims.

Master J4 (Tier 3 grade >= B on >= 80% of graded coordination runs): voice/quality of a coordination run can only be judged by Tier 3 grading, so this assertion defers (skipped, not failed) until the record carries a grade, then requires grade B or better. The >= 80% pass-rate threshold across runs is applied by the Stage 3 rollup, not by this per-record check.

The step-01.5 calendar pull (dedicated calendar subagent) wrote the unified calendar file that every downstream consumer (step-02 Task G, meeting prep, morning briefing) reads from disk instead of calling M365.

Regression guard: step-01.5 must end with the return-to-coordinator handoff, not a read-and-follow chain into step-02. The next-step chain is what let the 2026-10-22 calendar subagent walk the whole boot workflow (eval-20261022T114429-OCSJIC, 6.27M tokens) instead of exiting after one M365 call. If this trips, someone reintroduced the chain.

Regression guard: workflow.md must keep step-01.5 dispatched as its own tightly-briefed single-purpose subagent (one M365 call, no persona load, explicit workflows/boot/workflow.md reference for eval attribution). If this trips, the dispatch collapsed back into the walk-everything boot subagent.

Regression guard: step-01.2 must end with the return-to-coordinator handoff, not a read-and-follow chain into step-02. Part of the 2026-10-22 steps-02-04 context-tax fix (work-20261022-182004): one long-lived boot subagent walking steps 01.2-08 carried 500-720k input tokens per step for outputs of a few hundred tokens (eval-20261021T151330-QNQLC5, eval-20261013T114019-Q5UJLE). If this trips, someone reintroduced the chain.

Regression guard: step-01.2 must not contain a 'Read fully and follow' next-step chain. The chain is what let subagents walk the whole boot workflow instead of exiting after their single-purpose mandate.

Regression guard: step-02 must end with the return-to-coordinator handoff, not a read-and-follow chain into step-03. Eval evidence for the fix: eval-20261021T151330-QNQLC5 step-02 carried 545,309 input tokens for a 628-token output; eval-20261013T114019-Q5UJLE attributed 719,033 in / 4,291 out across the same steps. If this trips, someone reintroduced the chain.
Regression guard: step-02 must not contain a 'Read fully and follow' next-step chain.

Regression guard: step-03 must end with the return-to-coordinator handoff, not a read-and-follow chain into step-04. Eval evidence: eval-20261021T151330-QNQLC5 step-03 carried 495,386 input tokens for a 1,014-token output. If this trips, someone reintroduced the chain.
Regression guard: step-03 must not contain a 'Read fully and follow' next-step chain.

Regression guard: step-04 must end with the return-to-coordinator handoff, not a read-and-follow chain into step-05. Eval evidence: eval-20261021T151330-QNQLC5 step-04 carried 531,500 input tokens for a 1,354-token output. If this trips, someone reintroduced the chain.
Regression guard: step-04 must not contain a 'Read fully and follow' next-step chain.

Regression guard: workflow.md must keep steps 01.2, 02, 03, and 04 dispatched as their own tightly-briefed single-purpose subagents (no persona/SYSTEM.md load, explicit workflows/boot/workflow.md reference for eval attribution, Edit-not-Bash state updates), with the briefing subagent covering only steps 05-08.
